International Mother Language Day.fact: The day is also observed by Indian Bengalis in the states of West Bengal, Assam, Jharkhand, and Tripura, as well as in the union territory of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and diaspora communities.  == History == 21 February was declared to be International Mother Language Day by UNESCO on 17 November 1999.  It has been observed throughout the world since 21 February 2000.  The declaration came up in tribute to the Language Movement done by the Bangladeshis (then the East Pakistanis).  When Pakistan was created in 1947, it had two geographically separate parts: East Pakistan (currently known as Bangladesh) and West Pakistan (currently known as Pakistan).  The two parts were very different from each other in the sense of culture and language, and were also separated by India in between.
